newsitem.title: USA: Congress votes gold medal for Frank Sinatra.
newsitem.headline: Congress votes gold medal for Frank Sinatra.

text.p: Singer Frank Sinatra, who 30 years ago appeared before Congress to deny links with organised crime, on Tuesday was voted to receive a congressional gold medal.
The House of Representatives cleared the bill for President Bill Clinton on a voice vote. The Senate passed the legislation in February.
New York Democrat Jose Serrano, the chief sponsor of the bill, said he became a fan after learning to speak English as a child in Puerto Rico by listening to Sinatra's records.
"It is my way of saying thank you to this individual who brought so much joy to the world with his talent," said Serrano. He said he had 290 Sinatra records.
"Frank Sinatra is perhaps the greatest singer of popular American music of this century," added Representative Mike Castle, a Delaware Republican.

Serrano's press secretary said Serrano spoke to Sinatra's daughter, Nancy, after the vote. She told him Sinatra watched the debate with family members on television and was "in tears" after the bill passed.

In Los Angeles, Sinatra's publicist Susan Reynolds quoted the 81-year-old entertainer as saying: "When I started out at the Rustic Cabin (a roadhouse in New Jersey) as a waiter, I certainly didn't think I'd be honoured by the United States Congress!"
"Today, as a proud American, Congress may have brought a tear to my eyes, but that lofty institution has also made me very, very happy," she quoted him as saying.

When called before Congress, Sinatra accused members of the House Select Committee on Crime of indecent and irresponsible action in allowing an admitted murderer to deliver hearsay evidence linking him with the Mafia.

Sinatra, known in the entertainment industry as "The Chairman of the Board," lost his Nevada gambling license in 1963 after a Mafia boss, Sam Giancana, was seen in the Cal-Neva Lodge gambling casino in which Sinatra then held a major interest. The license was restored in 1981.
Serrano said his bill had 303 co-sponsors among the 435 House members. The bill authorises up to $30,000 for the cost of providing the medal.
Congress has approved 125 gold medals for prominent Americans including entertainers Bob Hope, John Wayne and Danny Thomas.
Sinatra has also received the Presidential Medal of Freedom. He was hospitalized in January after a heart attack, but returned home after eight days.
